Nintendo confirmed that NS2 hardware sales fell 37% year-on-year in the first half of this fiscal year, while software sales increased 18.8%. In addition to the fading dividends during the first explosive period, the decline in sales is also related to the increase in host prices caused by rising material costs. Although net sales in the first half of the fiscal year fell 12.1% year-on-year to 966 billion yen, Nintendo's operating profit still increased 49.1% to 216.5 billion yen. In the three months ended September 30, Nintendo sold a total of 2.67 million NS2 units and 15.04 million NS2 games. Throughout the first half of the fiscal year, NS2 hardware shipped 6.49 million units. In the first half of the fiscal year, net profit also increased by 11.0% to 220.9 billion yen

The more you watch and play, you will always encounter some weirdos, such as "Dandelion Unyielding" which was released in September this year. At first glance, when you first see "Dandelion Unyielding", you can easily regard it as a narrative, "small but beautiful" solo game. The art is small and fresh, the music is soft and soothing, a dandelion seed flies in the wind, and finally falls to the ground on the asphalt road, taking root with a little soil in the gap and growing with difficulty. After landing, what the player has to do is to collect water, sunlight and carbon dioxide, and make the dandelion grow through photosynthesis.

I would like to try putting "Watch the action" and "Think about the next step" on the same page, so that the action can be paused, rewinded, and taken apart for observation. [Introduction to 405 Game Podcast] "405 Game" is a podcast that has long-term focus on interactive entertainment and technological changes. We discuss games, but not just the game itself; we focus on AI, but not just model parameters. What we are more concerned about is - when technology leaps, how will entertainment be rewritten? The key instrument of this boss battle song is the guqin, especially its sliding strings, which perfectly reproduces Hua Qianxiao's "Drunken Sword" move on the auditory level. Moreover, because it is a folk instrument, it naturally has an ancient style, or martial arts temperament. But what I find most interesting is the style of this piece. It sounds like a trap-style hip-hop beat - the guqin plays the role of a sample. You can even imagine yourself doing a freestyle on this song.
